title: Unibranchness of a local ring is equivalent to its henselization having a unique minimal prime

standard_prerequisites.name: The henselization is flat over the ring, so going down computes the minimal primes of the ring from those of the henselization, and the henselization of a quotient is the quotient of the henselization by the image of the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the minimal prime below the unique minimal prime of the henselization and shows that the latter is the extension of the former.

standard_prerequisites.name: An integral ring map satisfies going up, so every maximal ideal of the integral closure lies over the maximal ideal of the base
standard_prerequisites.use: Restricts the primes to consider when checking whether the integral closure is local.

standard_prerequisites.name: A henselian local ring with a residue field extension having at least two maximal ideals splits the algebra as a product of at least two local rings, and an etale localization of an integral extension is again normal
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the contradiction in the first direction and the normality of the tensor product in the second.

core_obligations: Assume the henselization has a unique minimal prime and let the corresponding minimal prime of the ring be its contraction; use flatness and going down to see that this is the unique minimal prime of the ring, and use the quotient description of the henselization to see that the unique minimal prime is the extension of it (proof lines 31268-31276).

Let the integral closure of the quotient by that prime be considered and suppose it is not local: choose two distinct maximal ideals and elements separating them, and find a finite subalgebra of the integral closure whose two contractions are still distinct (proof lines 31277-31287).

Tensor this finite subalgebra with the flat henselization: display the chain of inclusions placing it inside the fraction field of the henselization, and use that the residue field of the tensor product has at least two maximal ideals together with the henselian property to split the tensor product as a product of at least two local rings, contradicting that it is a subring of a domain (proof lines 31288-31308).

For the converse, assume the ring is unibranch and take a local map to a local ring inducing an isomorphism of residue fields which is the localization of an etale algebra; show that the base changed integral closure is local and normal, hence a domain, so the quotient of the target by the image of the prime is a domain and the target has a unique minimal prime, and conclude for the henselization as a filtered colimit of such rings (proof lines 31310-31335).
proof_roadmap: First direction: reduce to proving that the integral closure of the quotient is local, and derive a contradiction from a finite subalgebra whose tensor product with the henselization splits (proof lines 31268-31308).

Second direction: use a local etale localization with trivial residue field extension to show that the base changed integral closure is a local normal domain, hence that the target has a unique minimal prime (proof lines 31310-31331).
Pass from the colimit description of the henselization to the henselization itself (proof lines 31331-31335).
difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes unibranchness of a local ring by the henselization having a unique minimal prime (statement lines 31248-31259). The proof gives a direct argument in both directions: a unique minimal prime in the henselization is pulled back by flatness to a unique minimal prime of the ring, and a finite subalgebra of the integral closure of the corresponding quotient is tensored with the henselization so that the henselian property would split it as a product of local rings although it sits inside a domain, which is the contradiction; conversely a local etale localization with trivial residue field extension is used to show that the base changed integral closure is a local normal domain, whence the target has a unique minimal prime, and the henselization is reached as a filtered colimit of such rings (proof lines 31261-31336). The splitting argument in the first direction and the normality argument in the second are the two technical cores.
